name: When is it more economical to repair my roof instead of replacing it?

mainEntity.name: When is it more economical to repair my roof instead of replacing it?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is generally more economical to repair your roof when the damage is localized, minor, and the roof is still within the first two-thirds of its expected lifespan. Examples include fixing a small leak, replacing a few missing shingles, or repairing isolated storm damage. If the repair cost exceeds 25-30% of a full replacement, or if the roof is nearing the end of its typical lifespan (e.g., 15+ years for asphalt shingles), replacement often offers better long-term value. We can help you weigh these cost considerations during your assessment.
acceptedAnswer.description: Repair is more economical for localized, minor damage on a roof still within the first two-thirds of its lifespan, otherwise replacement might be better.
